summary: Sacks is skeptical of the Uber/Expedia cross-sell thesis, arguing Uber users have no intent to book hotels through a ride-hailing app, making the synergy rationale MBA hand-waving rather than real product thinking.
quote: I don't think Uber customers want to be cross-sold on booking a hotel... when I use the Uber app, I just want to basically make a couple of clicks, set my destination, get my car, and then move on.

summary: Chamath argues that Uber acquiring Expedia for ~$30B would be a disastrously bad use of capital, as AI agents will commoditize travel UI layers and Uber would be better served by acquiring real defensible assets like Waymo.
quote: Why don't they just buy Waymo? Why don't they just go to Google and give them $30 billion of Uber stock and just carve in Waymo. Isn't that a better idea?

summary: Chamath highlights Perplexity's new agentic checkout concept as evidence that AI agents will disintermediate travel booking UIs, implying Perplexity is positioned to capture transaction flow currently owned by companies like Expedia.
quote: Perplexity launched something this week... it's basically a checkout concept. So you tell Perplexity what you would like it to buy, and then it will go and complete the transaction for you.
